study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modelling of brain function abnormalities in complex pathology needs the whole brain

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study exclusively used rsfMRI data from UK Biobank (N>60,000 people). From this dataset, 46,000 subjects without brain diagnoses were used for the normative model, divided into training (N=32,000) and test (N=14,000) groups. Additionally, subjects with bipolar disorder (N=101) and Parkinson's disease (N=132) were used for disease prediction evaluation.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We use rsfMRI time series data from the UK-Biobank, which contains rsfMRI data from more than 60k subjects. 46,000 subjects without brain diagnoses (International Classification of Disease 10 (ICD-10) category F and G) were used for the normative model in an approximately 70:30 train-test split (32,000 for training the model, 14,000 subjects for out-of-sample testing). For disease prediction, we used data from subjects with BD (ICD-10 F31, N=101) and PD (ICD-10 G20, N=132)."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Kobbersmed2025.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Data, L205-L207

answer.UK Biobank: normative model training (N=32,000 healthy), normative model testing (N=14,000 healthy), and clinical disease prediction evaluation (BD N=101, PD N=132)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: UK Biobank was used for three purposes: (1) Training the FUNCOIN normative model with 32,000 healthy subjects; (2) Testing the model's out-of-sample performance with 14,000 healthy subjects; (3) Evaluating the model's ability to identify brain disease in subjects with bipolar disorder (N=101) and Parkinson's disease (N=132).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "We divide the subjects into three groups: A large group of healthy subjects to train the model on (training data, N=32,000), a set of healthy subjects on which we test the out-of-sample performance of the model (test data, N=14,000), and a group of subjects with psychiatric or neurological diagnoses."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Kobbersmed2025.pdf.md: Results / Whole-brain normative modelling of FC, L103-L105

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single FUNCOIN normative model was developed. The overall healthy control sample comprised 46,000 subjects without brain diagnoses (ICD-10 category F and G). These were split approximately 70:30 into training (N=32,000) and test (N=14,000) sets.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "46,000 subjects without brain diagnoses (International Classification of Disease 10 (ICD-10) category F and G) were used for the normative model in an approximately 70:30 train-test split (32,000 for training the model, 14,000 subjects for out-of-sample testing)"
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Kobbersmed2025.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Data, L205-L207

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The paper only reports the minimum (44.56 years) and maximum (85.43 years) age values for the entire dataset. These values were used to linearly transform the age variable to the interval [0,1] for model fitting. Mean, SD, median, and IQR are not reported. The age range applies to the overall dataset; specific values for training vs. test phases are not separately reported.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "The age variable was linearly transformed the interval [0,1], with 0 and 1 corresponding to the minimum and maximum age in the whole dataset (44.56 and 85.43 years)."
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.location: Kobbersmed2025.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Model fitting, L251-L253

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex was included as a covariate in the model (coded as categorical variable with 0 denoting female, 1 denoting male), but the specific numbers or proportions of males and females in the healthy control sample are not reported in the paper.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Sex was coded as a categorical variable with 0 denoting female, 1 denoting male."
